title: An Evaluation Framework for National AI Regulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.15417v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Governments use laws, institutions, funding programs and nonbinding guidance to shape how AI is developed and used. Comparing these national approaches is difficult. A binding rule and a detailed voluntary framework can address the same problem but create different duties. The resources needed to carry them out also differ by jurisdiction. This paper develops an evaluation framework for the documented design and implementation readiness of national AI policy. The comparison covers China, India, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, the United Kingdom and the United States. The European Union is included as a supranational comparator. The framework evaluates a versioned portfolio of official instruments rather than one prominent law or strategy. Its criteria ask whether the portfolio governs serious AI risks and whether responsible institutions can implement its commitments. translated_title: 国家人工智能监管评估框架
translated_abstract: 政府通过法律、机构、资助计划和非约束性指导来塑造人工智能的开发和使用方式。比较这些国家方法较为困难。一项具有约束力的规则和一个详细的自愿框架可能解决相同的问题，但会产生不同的义务。执行这些措施所需的资源也因司法管辖区而异。本文开发了一个评估框架，用于评估国家人工智能政策的文档化设计和实施准备情况。比较范围涵盖中国、印度、日本、新加坡、韩国、英国和美国。欧盟作为超国家比较对象被纳入。该框架评估一个版本化的官方工具组合，而非单一突出法律或战略。其标准询问该组合是否治理了严重的人工智能风险，以及负责任机构能否实施其承诺。它们还考察了人工智能生命周期中的覆盖范围以及可用的保护措施。
tldr: 本文提出了一个评估国家人工智能政策组合的设计与实施准备度的框架，并比较了七个国家及欧盟的监管覆盖范围和风险治理能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an evaluation framework for assessing the design and implementation readiness of national AI policy portfolios, comparing seven countries and the EU in terms of regulatory coverage and risk governance.
